newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 3.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.

-- BROWN NAMES BANK ADVISERS

UK chancellor Gordon Brown has appointed Professor Charles Goodhart of the London School of Economics, Professor William Butler of Cambridge University, Sir Alan Bud, DeAnne Julius, chief economist at British Airways to help set UK interest rates on the Bank of England's new monetary policy committee. The appointments are a further move in the transfer of interest rate control from the treasury to the Bank.
-- CAMELOT BONUS PAY SETTLEMENT REJECTED BY SMITH

The dispute between the UK government and Camelot over bonus payments to the lottery company's directors rose another level on Monday as National Heritage secretary Chris Smith rejected the company's settlement proposals. Camelot had offered to donate to charities the same amount of money it had promised its directors and also examined the possibility of turning the lottery into a non-profit operation.
-- FRANC, D-MARK DROP ON WORRIES OVER EMU

With the Socialist victory in France and the recent turmoil in Germany over the revaluing of gold revenues, the franc and mark tumbled on foreign exchange markets on Monday, and anxiety mounted in Germany concerning a possible broader-based and weaker European monetary union. The EC's president Jacques Santer said there was "no possibility" for a delay in the launch of Emu beyond January 1, 1999.
-- UTILITY URGES BROWN TO LIMIT WINDFALL LEVY

John Devaney, chairman of UK electricity company Eastern Group, has requested that the Treasury base any windfall tax levies on gains made by shareholders during the first year of a company's privatisation. Devaney added the tax should apply to British Telecom and British Gas GAS.L as well as National Power and PowerGen, stating that BT has "a virtual monopoly network".
-- TELECOMS GROUP CREATES 400 JOBS AS DEMAND RISES

GPT, the largest telecommunications equipment manufacturer in the UK, is to create 400 new jobs in the country in response to increased international demand for advanced transmission systems. GPT is 60 percent owned by GEC and 40 percent controlled by Siemens of Germany. Earlier in the week, GPT won a 3 million stg Lattelekom contract to supply payphones, management systems and smart telephone cards.
-- EMAP PROFITS JUMP TO 121 MILLION STG

Media and exhibitions group Emap has reported a 40 percent leap in annual pre-tax profits to 121.1 million stg excluding exceptional items. The results were boosted by advertising growth in the UK magazine and radio markets, and were achieved
on sales up 23 percent at 741.6 million stg.
-- CHINA, TURKEY PLAN EUROBONDS

China and Turkey are both planning to join the list of high-profile emerging market issuers to offer bonds denominated in German marks. The move will provide a fillip for the German bond market ahead of the expected launch of European monetary union in 1999. The Turkish launch is expected this week, and is likely to be 1 billion marks (357 million stg).
-- WHITBREAD PAYS 14,000 STG DEBT

Brewing group Whitbread has paid a 14,000 stg debt in order to avoid a High Court winding-up petition. The action, brought by a Surrey businessman trading as DTR Network Services, sought to have Whitbread's businesses, including 3,850 pubs, closed down over the debt. The case will still be heard on Wednesday, but after payment of the debt, solicitors for the businessman will not proceed with seeking a winding-up order.
-- IOC FINDS A KEY TO GROWTH

British firm Integrated Optical Components, which develops and manufactures components critical to the transmission of telecommunications signals along optical fibre cables, has almost doubled its interim pre-tax profits to 411,000 stg. The company, which believes it holds a world lead in the technology, floated on the Alternative Investment Market in March last year.
-- JD SPORTS HIT BY UNSOLD STOCK

Shares in John Davies Sports fell 18 percent on Monday following a warning from the sportswear retailer that serious stock problems would wipe out any chances of recording like-for-like sales growth this year. The slump in the share price came despite JD Sports reporting a 43 percent increase in pre-tax profits for the year to March 31, from 6.71 million stg to 9.62 million stg.
